messages:
noah: thinking aloud: what if the edge merges very similar read requests into one upstream call and fans results back? saves tokens but worries about streaming resume + side effects.

jia: cool for read-only paths. If you want to do it for anything with side-effects you need per-subrequest idempotency tokens. otherwise duplicates are risky.

matt: Agreed. Two-mode approach: default-only-read, opt-in headers for teams that want full semantics. opt-in requires upstream to echo per-sub accounting and resume checkpoints.

irene: Streaming detail: we must track per-substream resume indexes (kv-cache offsets). even if we merge, each logical client needs a resume token if upstream aborts midstream. that means more in-memory state during the coalesce window.

noah: prototype knobs: coalesce_window_ms=8, max_coalesce_inflight=256, attach X-Sub-Ids header. if mem_gauge > threshold, fallback to passthrough for that route for 30s.

jia: metrics: coalesce_attempts, coalesce_active_subs, coalesce_mem_bytes, coalesce_fallback_count, per_sub_resume_emitted. export as counters+histograms.

matt: billing: start with proportional split by prompt length, but prefer upstream per-sub token counts when available. document the method.

irene: failure mode: upstream sends partial tokens and closes without checkpoints -> safest is to fail all subs rather than risk inconsistent state.

deploy-bot: deploy: edge/proxy/multiplex-safe v0.1 -> succeeded in staging (2025-06-10T04:12:01Z)

noah: i'll open a short RFC with config names and the opt-in header schema (X-Sub-Id, X-Resume-Mode). also add a tiny curl example for the read route so QA can load-test. thanks for the quick feedback.
